title: Code review: models modal and role assignment scopes (real production diff, seeded defects)

defects.title: Assignable-step roster drops workflow-internal steps, and the modal's slot list then prunes their saved assignments
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that getAssignableSteps filters on step["user-invocable"] in addition to the skills exclusion, and that this roster is the modal's step list: create-dialog-modals.tsx passes it as deps.steps, use-model-modal builds selectionSlots from it with buildRoleSlots, and those slots become the slots field of the modelAssignments query. listModelAssignments feeds deps.slots to pruneStaleConfigSections, which calls pruneStaleConfig with ConfigValidity.roleIds, and writer.ts patchPrunedConfig deletes every [roles."step.<id>"] section whose role id is not in that set. Opening the models modal therefore erases the saved model and effort of every workflow-internal step from the global config, and those steps also vanish from Workflow Overrides although they still run under their own slot. Naming only 'internal steps disappear from the list' without the config-pruning consequence does not count.

defects.title: Step-agent slot resolution prefers the global persona role over the step-scoped assignment
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that resolveSlotRole now returns roles.get(agentRole) ?? roles.get(slot.roleId) for step-agent slots, so the global persona role shadows the more specific step.<definitionId>.agent.<role> assignment in every config-side path that uses resolveSlotRole (listModelAssignments row model and effort, listEffortOptionsForSlot's current effort, ensureConcreteRoleAssignments), while resolveSubagentRole in the same file still prefers the step-scoped slot at runtime. The modal therefore displays and edits a different model than the subagent actually runs with, and a per-step override appears not to save. Naming 'the precedence changed' without stating that the specific slot must win over the global fallback, or without the modal/runtime divergence, does not count.

defects.title: Effort options for an inherit selection are computed from the model being abandoned
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that listEffortOptionsForSlot computes effectiveModel as model ?? resolved.model instead of model ?? stepWorker.model, that model === null is exactly the inherit selection, and that an inheriting slot runs on the step-worker's model, not on the model resolveSlotRole still reports for the slot. The effort list is therefore built by effortOptionsForModel for the outgoing model: the user can save xhigh or max against an inherited model that does not declare those tiers, or is denied tiers the inherited model does support, while the inherit row label still reads the step-worker effort. Naming 'inherit handling looks off' without the model === null / step-worker relationship does not count.

defects.title: Scope availability is captured once at hook creation instead of tracking the foreground session
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that scopeToggleAvailable is no longer a memo over deps.foregroundSessionId() but a constant captured while useModelModal runs, and that createDialogModals builds this hook once as the shell mounts, before any session tab exists, so the captured value stays false for the process lifetime. Consequence: toggleScope returns early so 'g' never switches scope, the scope help hint never renders, and openModelsModal still reads deps.foregroundSessionId() live, so the modal opens in session scope with no way back to defaults. Naming only 'a memo became a plain function' without the stale-capture consequence does not count.

defects.title: groupIdForSlot treats step-agent slots as top-level, silently dropping their inherit saves
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that groupIdForSlot returns undefined for step-agent slots even though isStepSlot is true for them, and trace at least one consequence in use-model-modal.ts: saveEffort's guard `if (model === null && !groupIdForSlot(slot)) return` discards the Inherit selection for a step subagent row with no toast and no error, although listModelOptionsForSlot renders a selectable inherit row for every step slot; and returnViewForSlot/itemsForSlot send the user to the top-level list instead of back into the Workflow Overrides group after editing a subagent row, while modalTitle loses the group segment that disambiguates the identical subagent labels. Naming only 'the grouping changed' does not count.

defects.title: Session-scope save no longer refreshes the foreground role snapshot
defects.catch_criteria: The review must identify that saveEffort calls deps.onSnapshotChanged only when result.mirrored is true, and that mirrored is set only on the compound defaults-and-session path in model-assignment-service.ts while a session-scope save returns just { label }. The one scope that changes the live tab's roles therefore stops refreshing the foreground role snapshot, so the prompt bar and footer keep showing the previous model after a session-scope save. Naming 'a condition was simplified' without the fact that mirrored is only set for compound writes does not count.

review_prompt_hint: The change reshapes the models modal: the Subagents group is removed so global agent roles (Reviewer, Explorer, Implementer) sit at the top level next to Chat and the renamed Steps role, the step group becomes Workflow Overrides, skills are excluded from the model-assignable step roster, and chat-only system-prompt guidance is regrouped. Pay close attention to model-assignment slot construction and which slots the modal sends to orchestration, role resolution precedence between step-scoped and global roles, inherit semantics for models and efforts, SolidJS reactivity and scope handling in the modal hook, and what each save path must refresh
